lukmanier-oberalp-vorderrhein-high-roads.slogan: Two passes, one river valley and a proper touring spine.
lukmanier-oberalp-vorderrhein-high-roads.story: Two passes, one river valley and a proper touring spine. Out of Chur and back again: 333 km, roughly 6 h 24 in the saddle. On the way it passes Andermatt and Disentis. The climbs: Lukmanier pass road and Oberalppass high road. It tops out at 2,044 m. Lukmanier Pass is subject to seasonal closure - check it is open before you set off. The passes are the reason to go.

scenicChapters.title: Chur fuel gate → Lukmanier pass road
scenicChapters.narrative: The ground tilts up and stays tilted for 136 km. 1322 m of it, taken steadily rather than in one wall — a steady rhythm suits this better than bursts. The height arrives whether you hurry or not.

scenicChapters.title: Furka Pass
scenicChapters.narrative: The last of the trees go and the road runs out onto open ground. The summit sits at 1915 m, and what surrounds it is rock, weather and distance. Cold comes early up here and stays late. Ride it with something in reserve: the summit is not the end of the work, only the middle of it.
scenicChapters.riderNote: Check the pass is open before you commit to it.

scenicChapters.title: Furka Pass
scenicChapters.narrative: First and second gear more often than not. Look through each corner to the next one and let the engine do the holding. The valley floor is behind you and the road starts working for its height at about 7.5%. Corners stack above one another where the ground allows nothing straighter.

scenicChapters.title: Furka-Grimsel-Susten Pass Loop
scenicChapters.narrative: 31 km that neither climbs nor drops much. The road settles into the ground rather than fighting it — this is where a day makes up time without anyone trying. Third and fourth, and very little else.

scenicChapters.title: Grand Tour of Switzerland
scenicChapters.narrative: For 56 km this is Grand Tour of Switzerland, a road with a name of its own and a reason for it. Expect company on a summer weekend. Early is better than fast.
